Fixes bug B-next-ready-over-held-files: ddflow next --phase P-config-engine printed 'Ready (1 ready, 0 running)' with CE-defaults-file and its writes, no conflict shown; the claim straight after was refused because .ddflow/pins.toml is held by sw-quotameters on B-quota-meters (live, renewed 100 s before). ddflow_next promises the reason for everything that may not start, and lanes are told to check next before a claim since a repeated refused claim can auto-approve. Found on CE-defaults-file.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-next-ready-over-held-files --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-next-ready-over-held-files --regression-test <test>` first).

chunk_findings.detail: The catalog’s own rule is that a field it cannot name stays empty and is never guessed, and that each `checks` entry grades the feature. `session-start-brief` and `key-by-env-name` set `descriptor_fields = []` and still cite `checks = ["facts"]`, while the notes say the descriptor has no field for the brief path and that key env names live only in modelreg / models.toml. Given a harness with no session-start brief and no key-env knob, `facts` only inspects descriptor facts, so both rows grade as covered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/catalog.toml:34

chunk_findings.detail: `lean-tool-profile` is answered by `mcp.path` and `mcp.shape`, but the note says the lean profile is the ddflow-side `[mcp].tools` knob and those fields only name registration. A descriptor that registers MCP and ships the full tool list still satisfies `checks = ["facts"]`, so the offline grade does not fail a non-lean profile.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/catalog.toml:26

chunk_findings.detail: A row with no grading check and no descriptor field is accepted. Given `[[in_agent]] feature = "session_ingest"`, `descriptor_fields = []`, `checks = []` (title/note omitted), `load()` returns a `Row` with empty `checks` and `descriptor_fields`. That is wrong because every catalog feature must name the descriptor field(s) that answer it and at least one offline conformance check; an empty row is treated as a valid feature and cannot be graded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/catalog.py:_parse_row

chunk_findings.detail: Check ids are not resolved against the live declared-check modules the module claims to reuse, and a non-string id is not a `CatalogError`. `DECLARED_CHECKS` / `FIXED_CHECKS` / `LANE_CHECK` are hardcoded literals; nothing imports `tests/harness_conformance.declared` (or `driver_conformance` / swarm conformance) to confirm the id still exists. Input `checks = ["brand_new_declared_kind"]` is rejected even when that kind is already declared, so the catalog cannot record a reused check without a code edit. Input `checks = [1]` raises `AttributeError` on `cid.startswith` instead of `CatalogError`, so a malformed row escapes the loader contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/catalog.py:known_check

chunk_findings.detail: Managed-record history is not tied to the rows. A feature may be loaded with no `[[history]]` entry, an `action = "retire"` entry may coexist with that feature still in `rows`, and a history `feature` need not match any row. Given an `in_agent` row `feature = "trust_handling"` with `checks = ["facts"]` and either no history or `[[history]] feature = "trust_handling" action = "retire" date = "2026-01-01"`, `load()` succeeds. That is wrong for add/edit/retire records: a retired slug stays active, and a live slug can have no ledger.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/catalog.py:load

chunk_findings.detail: `assert "lane" in cited and CF.CHECKS` never checks that any conformance level is actually cited. With `cited` containing the token `"lane"` (plus `"facts"` and `"hooks"`) and `CF.CHECKS` any non-empty collection that does not intersect `cited` — for example `{"1","2","3","4","5","6","7"}` — the assertion still passes, so a catalog that omits levels 1–7 is graded as reusing them.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_parity_catalog.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: The reuse pin for declared hook checks never loads `tests/harness_conformance/declared.py`. `any(c.startswith("hook:") and c.partition(":")[2] in HR.CANONICAL_EVENTS ...)` is true for a forged id such as `hook:` plus any string already in `HR.CANONICAL_EVENTS`, and `test_lane_and_declared_check_modules_exist_and_are_the_single_owner` only asserts `HR.CANONICAL_EVENTS`, `CF.CHECKS`, and `C.FIXED_CHECKS`. Deleting or emptying `tests/harness_conformance/declared.py` leaves both tests green, so the catalog can cite checks that module does not own.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_parity_catalog.py:62
